newsitem.title: USA: Flood-hit Arizona Indian reservation evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Flood-hit Arizona Indian reservation evacuated.

text.p: Helicopters worked to evacuate as many as 400 tourists and residents from a remote canyon on an Indian reservation in northwestern Arizona on Sunday after floods swept through the area, officials said.

Authorities estimated that 200 to 300 tourists - many there for the annual Peach Festival activities - would have to be plucked from the Havasupai Indian Reservation following heavy rains that hit the area Sunday morning.

Another 100 residents of Supai Village also were flooded out of their homes southwest of the Grand Canyon when a creek became swollen with water, according to Bob McNichols, a superintendent with the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
It was not immediately clear how many homes were flooded in the area, which is accessible only by hiking, mules or helicopters. The nearest road is eight miles away.

Five helicopters from the National Guard, state and tribal agencies were on scene aiding in the evacuation. A shelter also was set up at a gymnasium about 70 miles away for those forced to leave their homes, authorities said.

McNichols said he was unsure whether there would be the need for any additional evacuations from the 600-person village, a picturesque spot visited by thousands each year. The flooding affected water and sewer services.
"We've got a lot of work to do," McNichols told Reuters. "We're getting a handle on this as we speak."

This is the third time in seven years that the area has seen major floods, with the others occurring in 1990 and 1993. All three times, runoff from Cataract Creek rushed through the small village causing severe damage.
